title: Animal re-identification via MegaDescriptor (BVRA): third-stage body-embedding model after VM1+VM2, mirroring face_recognition pattern for people
author: jill (operator-directed 2026-09-14, post dog-enrollment + body-scan discussion)
plan_section: v2 animal pipeline completion: enroll operator animals + third-stage embedding model (MegaDescriptor-L-384) for individual animal re-identification, paralleling how face_recognition runs on people after VM1+VM2
trigger: Operator 2026-09-14 (verbatim): 'So here is what I am thinking, we already have a well-established pipeline and I do not want to mess with this. I mean, I do not want to mess with changing YOLO vision model 1 or vision model 2, but just like with people, we are going to do basically a third run through of a model and that will be the facial recognition, then with dogs, we can do a third or I guess a fourth run through of the model on this Bohemian animal thing. So it would basically be another add on to the pipeline on the animal branch. So yeah, create some PRD stories for after we get the detailed description of the animal from the VM2 that we then run it into the Bohemian to see if we can recognize enrolled animals.' Two concrete gaps: (1) v2 listener/pipeline.py Stage 12 only matches vehicles + persons - animal mode falls through with no match and no TG3. (2) No animal embedding model exists, so even if we add an animal branch, we have no way to re-identify THIS dog across many alerts vs. some other similar dog.
background: v2 currently has no animal matching at all. v1 (farm-surveillance-refactor) had a feature-weighted ensemble matcher (animal_matcher.py + animal_schema.py) that scored candidates on distinctive_features + coat_primary_color + body_size + body_build + face_details + coat_pattern + estimated_age + sex_signal. That approach worked but required VM2 to emit a stable, multi-field structured output that often varied alert-to-alert (subjective descriptions). The operator wants a third-model approach (analog to face_recognition for people) that produces a deterministic 768-dim embedding from the cropped animal image and matches via cosine similarity. The chosen model is BVRA MegaDescriptor-L-384 (https://huggingface.co/BVRA/MegaDescriptor-L-384), an ArcFace-loss-trained CNN for animal re-identification, loaded via timm.create_model(hf-hub:BVRA/MegaDescriptor-L-384, pretrained=True). MegaDescriptor was trained on 49 species including dogs. Weights are downloaded at runtime into models/ (already stripped by scripts/release/config.yaml rules models/*.onnx + *.pt). Operator has confirmed: do NOT touch VM1 (YOLO) or VM2 (Qwen-VL) - the embedding model is a NEW third-stage that runs after VM2 returns the structured description + better_crop.

shipping_definition: (a) Pipeline Stage 12 routes animal mode to animal_matcher (was: fell through silently). (b) infra/animal_embedder.py loads MegaDescriptor-L-384 from local models/ via timm, computes 768-dim embedding for any 384x384+ PIL/np.ndarray input. (c) data/known/animals/known_animals.json + data/known/animals/embeddings.npz store per-animal metadata + per-image 768-dim vectors. (d) scripts/enroll_animal.py CLI: --name --id --images N jpegs saves entry + averages embeddings. (e) animal_matcher.match_animal() returns matched candidate dict + cosine score or matched:False. (f) US-044 match-alert pipeline reads animal matches correctly (depends on US-044c/d). (g) pytest green. (h) All six stories committed on main with US-045 in the message. Working tree clean.

design_principles: Mirror face_recognition pattern: VM1 (YOLO) detects bbox -> VM2 (Qwen-VL) returns structured description + better_crop -> ANIMAL_EMBEDDER (MegaDescriptor) on chosen crop -> cosine similarity vs enrolled embeddings.

Better crop selection: pipeline Stage 11b (NEW) reads vm2_result.better_crop, picks crop_a or crop_b accordingly. Falls back to crop_a when better_crop is absent or neither. US-044b builds the pick_alert_image_path() helper that US-045 reuses.

Embedding storage: numpy .npz file with named keys = animal ids, values = stacked 768-dim float32 arrays. Index file = known_animals.json with id + label + species + breed + color + first_enrolled_iso + sample_image_paths.
Cosine similarity: standard (A @ B) / (norm_A * norm_B). Threshold initial = 0.85, tuned in US-045f against historical alerts.

animal_matcher.match_animal() returns: {matched: True, candidate: {id, label, species, breed, color}, score: float, gap: float, runner_ups: [{id, score}, ...]} on hit, {matched: False, top_candidates: [{id, label, score}], threshold: float} on miss.
Test with synthetic embeddings first (numpy random) before plugging MegaDescriptor - keeps unit tests fast + CPU-only.
Single commit per story on main with US-045 in the message.

stories.title: Tune ANIMAL_MATCH_THRESHOLD against historical alerts (find embedding similarity distribution for known dogs vs other animals)
stories.scope: scripts/tune_animal_threshold.py: scan data/frames/ for historical alerts that VM2 classified as animal, pick the better_crop for each (using existing US-044a schema), embed each via MegaDescriptor-L-384, compute pairwise cosine similarity between all frames of the same camera within a 7-day window, print top 5 most-similar pairs + bottom 5 least-similar pairs. Update config.yaml with threshold default based on observed distribution. Output: docs/animal-threshold-tuning.md with recommended threshold + reasoning.
